title: The Plate Breakage After Mandibular Condylar Fracture Osteosynthesis
content: Despite continuous and significant development of fixation materials, plate breakage is still observed after osteosynthesis of the mandibular condyles. The aim of this study is to present the complication of fixation material breakage, hoping that it will trigger the development of new, more durable plates. 238 cases of plate use for osteosynthesis in this anatomical region were analyzed. Cases of compression screw use as the sole fixation material were excluded from the study. Plate breakage was found in 6 cases, which accounts for 2.52% of treated individuals. It seems that most plate breakages could be avoided by maintaining effective control over patients after surgery for up to 6 months. Risk factors for breakage were identified and guidelines for improving the design of future plates were provided. It appears that by analyzing some features of the plate design, it is possible to indicate the direction in which the design of stronger plates for osteosynthesis of mandibular condylar fractures should develop.
